oneLineRole: The cited evidence + single canonical home for the engine's verified reference numbers (Trinity/Bengen golden cases, MC calibration band, longevity formula, full tax surface) and the validation contract the engine is built and pinned against.

items.claim: This doc is the single-source home of the verified reference numbers: Trinity/Bengen golden cases, the Monte Carlo calibration band, the longevity formula, and the full tax surface (brackets, RMDs, senior-bonus deduction, Social-Security provisional-income taxation). The engine is built and pinned against these numbers and fully consumes this doc. Where a number lives, it lives HERE — never re-typed into a plan or component (single-source rule that prevents stat drift).
The healthcare half of the tax surface — ACA-PTC (pre-65), IRMAA (post-65), HSA — lives in its OWN note: docs/research/pre65-healthcare.md. Together the two are the engine's tax + health reference.

The load-bearing engine invariants (single shared market draw / CRN, stateless Box-Muller, reduce-to-spine, externally-derived fixtures) live ONCE in docs/architecture.md — this doc points to them, does not duplicate them.

Confidence tags must be preserved on purpose: do NOT flatten 'defensible' or 'directional' into 'verified.' A directional fixture is marked directional in code; the §0 exit-gate work pinned the ones that needed pinning.

THE LANDMINE THIS STRAND DEFUSED: the raw research designated a WRONG Trinity bond number as a golden oracle. Encoding it would have made a CORRECT engine fail its own tests. The verifier caught it; every golden number in this doc is the corrected one.

SOLVER VALIDATION CONTRACT (Act 4, still ahead, recorded so it cannot be rediscovered): because the product RECOMMENDS a strategy, the contract GROWS beyond 'the number is right' and needs three more case classes, all GATING before the solver is allowed to speak (a wrong recommended strategy costs real dollars).

Solver case class (a) Optimality / ranking oracle — hand-computable cases where the best drawdown/conversion order is KNOWN (conventional taxable→tax-deferred→Roth ordering; a textbook bracket-filling Roth optimum), so a confidently-wrong recommendation fails loud — the way Trinity/Bengen make 'the number is right' testable.

Solver case class (b) Ranking-stability under CRN — the RANKING (not just each pairwise delta) must be stable on the shared draw matrix or the recommendation jitters. Generalize the 2-arm CRN test to K candidate strategies → identical normals path-for-path across the survivor MFJ→single transition.

Solver case class (c) Grade calibration — 'just do it' must ACTUALLY be robust across the futures and 'coin-flip' ACTUALLY a coin-flip. The sole human gate (N=1 cold-read) judges a grade's TONE but is structurally unable to judge its CORRECTNESS, so this automated oracle is the only backstop on a tool moving real money.

items.claim: Optimizer's-curse correction (part of the contract): argmax over many candidates on ONE seed overfits that seed's noise → the in-sample winner's score is optimistically biased. Report graded confidence on an INDEPENDENT held-out seed-set (or paired top-K dispersion). Because directional-until-pinned fixtures decide the exact near-ties the optimizer overfits, PINNING THE TAX-REFERENCE PRIMARIES IS A HARD SOLVER PREREQUISITE, not a residual gate.

Trinity Study (Cooley/Hubbard/Walz 1998) vintage-lock: 1926–1995, S&P 500 + LONG-TERM CORPORATE bonds, inflation-adjusted withdrawals, success = balance > $0 at horizon end, annual rebalance. Golden success rates at 4% infl-adj / 30 yr: 50/50 = 95% (exact anchor); 75/25 = 100% (verifier fix — raw research said 98%); 100% stock = 98%; 100% bond = ~70% (CORRECTED — raw research said '20–35%' which is WRONG and was flagged a golden oracle). Full 100%-bond row at 3/4/5/6% = 94/70/51/44%.

The 100%-bond = ~70% row is the DIAGNOSTIC case: a correct engine with inflation-adjusted withdrawals must show bonds doing POORLY, not 'safe.' If the engine shows bonds safe, the inflation adjustment or volatility handling is wrong.

Bengen SAFEMAX = 4.15% corresponds to the 1966 retiree cohort (verifier fix — raw research mis-paired it with 1968). Allocation 50% S&P 500 / 50% INTERMEDIATE-TERM GOVERNMENT bonds, 30 yr, annual rebalance.

Bengen SAFEMAX is only bit-exact against Bengen's exact dataset (Ibbotson intermediate-government series). Without that dataset, treat as a DIRECTIONAL survive/fail test, not a golden number. Pin the dataset before calling it deterministic.

Bond-index mismatch: Trinity used CORPORATE bonds; Bengen used GOVERNMENT bonds → their numbers legitimately differ (Bengen 50/50 ≈ 100% vs Trinity 50/50 = 95% for the same 4%/30yr). NEVER cross-validate one against the other's exact figure.

Monte Carlo calibration is a BAND, not an equality: a pure i.i.d. Monte Carlo scores a given withdrawal rate MORE PESSIMISTICALLY than a historical backtest (i.i.d. draws ignore mean-reversion and can string arbitrarily bad runs). 4%/30yr lands high-80s to ~90%, BELOW the 95% historical. This is by design — assert only a RANGE for MC, use the historical cases as the exact oracle.
Pfau/Kitces: high-CAPE environments imply a 3–3.5% safe rate, not 4% — corroborates the 'deliberately conservative real returns' decision.

Volatility drag (the #1 MC bug): Geometric ≈ Arithmetic − σ²/2. For a lognormal sim use log-drift μ = arithmetic_mean − σ²/2, else you OVERSTATE compounding. Precise statement: feed the arithmetic mean but subtract σ²/2 as drift ('arithmetic-average growth, not compound' is the headline, σ²/2 is the mechanism). Unit test: +50% then −50% → two-year cumulative −25%, annualized geometric −13.4% (verifier relabel — don't conflate cumulative with annualized).

'Success' = $1 remaining HIDES magnitude. Also report terminal-value percentiles + depth-of-failure, not just pass/fail — this feeds the 'probability of adjustment' dollar-grammar (need the distribution, not a binary).

Longevity: use COHORT, not period life tables (period understates longevity). Joint-and-survivor must be DERIVED from single-sex curves: P(last survivor alive) = p_x + p_y − p_x·p_y. The engine must use SEX-SPECIFIC curves per spouse, never one rate for both; the longevity test asserts the couple figure = the formula on the two shipped curves, not a hardcoded constant. Independence is assumed — real spousal mortality is positively correlated, mildly overstating last-survivor probability, which errs safe for a survival floor. Do NOT model a fixed 'to-age-90' horizon — it systematically misstates ruin probability for a couple.

Grounded-search-era POPULATION longevity figures (since superseded by pinned cohorts): ~25% of 65-year-olds live past 90; ~53% chance at least one of a 65-yo couple reaches 90. The ~53% is NOT the symmetric ~25% applied to both (which yields 43.75% under p_x+p_y−p_x·p_y) — it reflects sex-differentiated cohort survival (women materially higher).

Younger cohorts survive materially longer than the population figures. Per-spouse curves and the couple anchor are encoded in src/engine/reference/mortality.ts. A Trustees-Report-vintage bump is a deliberate re-pin, never a silent refresh.

items.claim: THE FALSIFIABLE IN/OUT LINE: a tax/health effect is IN iff withdrawal sequencing or a conversion can MOVE it. IN: ordinary brackets, standard deduction, RMDs, SS-taxation, MFJ→single, ACA-PTC (pre-65), IRMAA (post-65), cap-gains / qualified-dividend stacking. OUT-but-disclosed: NIIT (3.8% surtax), state income tax. An omitted cliff INVERTS which strategy wins, not just its size — which is exactly why ACA-PTC and IRMAA come IN.
items.sourceSection: Tax reference intro / Engine tax+health scope

items.claim: TWO DISTINCT MAGI CALCULATORS are required (ACA-MAGI ≠ IRMAA-MAGI). A sequencing/conversion change shifts ACA-MAGI or IRMAA-MAGI across their cliffs.
items.sourceSection: Tax reference intro / Engine tax+health scope

items.claim: LEGISLATIVE LANDMINE: the enhanced ACA subsidies EXPIRED 12/31/2025, unre-enacted as of 2026-06-04 → model the 400% FPL cliff as the 2026 BASE CASE, expose 'enhanced' as a scenario toggle, re-verify EVERY BUILD (CI-gated by `pnpm verify:aca`).

items.claim: Tax-reference verification provenance: verified via gemini-grounding 2026-06-04 (Tax Foundation 2026 bracket tables; IRS RMD FAQ; SECURE 2.0; OBBBA; + the healthcare note's IRS/CMS primaries). The 2026 figures were grounded-search-verified and have since been pinned against the IRS primaries (see Pin-pass status).

LEGAL BASIS (itself a staleness-stamp fact): The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), signed 2025-07-04, made the TCJA individual rate structure (10/12/22/24/32/35/37) and the elevated standard deduction PERMANENT — so 2026 is NOT a TCJA-sunset reversion to pre-2018 brackets (TCJA individual provisions were set to expire 12/31/2025). Therefore the 'tax-table vintage' staleness clock does NOT track a one-time 2026 reversion; it tracks (a) annual inflation indexing of a permanent bracket structure, (b) the senior-bonus-deduction sunset, (c) the RMD-age step, and (d) any future law change. STAMP THE LEGAL BASIS (OBBBA-2025), not just the year, so a future statutory change is falsifiable rather than mistaken for inflation drift.

2026 MFJ standard deduction = $32,200. Single ≈ half (≈ $16,100 — pin exact against the IRS Rev. Proc.; 2025 was MFJ $31,500 / single $15,750, exactly 2×). Additional age-65+ standard deduction ≈ $1,650/spouse MFJ (2026) — supporting, pin exact.

Widow(er)'s-penalty mechanics: after the first death, an empty-nest retired couple files SINGLE the year AFTER (year of death = still MFJ; Qualifying-Surviving-Spouse MFJ-equivalent rates apply up to two following years ONLY with a dependent child in the home — which the target couple almost never has, so NO QSS grace — IRS Pub 501). The survivor's same real dollars then fall into ~half-width single brackets with ~half the standard deduction → the tax cliff converting-while-both-file-MFJ defuses. The joint→survivor two-regime boundary DOUBLES AS the MFJ→single filing-status switch — no new boundary.

RMD start age is birth-year-derived, NOT a flat 73 (SECURE 2.0): born ≤ 1950 → 72; born 1951–1959 → 73; born 1960 or later → 75 (the 75 step is effective 2033). The 1959 statutory drafting glitch resolves to 73 (current standard interpretation). RMD = IRS Uniform Lifetime Table divisor applied to the prior-year-end pre-tax balance; first RMD due by April 1 of the year after reaching RMD age.
The RMD age is a per-person function of birth year and is legislatively scheduled to change (the 2033 step) — so it is a vintage-stamped / birth-year-keyed input, never a hardcoded literal.

Temporary Senior Bonus Deduction (OBBBA): $6,000 per person age 65+ ($12,000 MFJ), on top of the standard deduction, claimable whether itemizing or not. MAGI phase-out begins single > $75k / MFJ > $150k, reduced 6% per dollar over. Deduction = $6,000 × (# spouses 65+) reduced by 6% of (MAGI − $150k) on a joint return. Fully gone: single > $175k; MFJ > $250k when ONE spouse is 65+ ($6k), but MFJ > $350k when BOTH are 65+ ($12k) — the both-65+ couple keeps it up to $350k MAGI. Source: IRS FS-2025-03; OBBBA P.L. 119-21 / H.R.1.

Senior-bonus KTD: a flat 'MFJ > $250k' phase-out is the one-spouse case ONLY and would overstate tax / understate conversion+IRMAA headroom in the $250–350k band — exactly where a conversion solver decides. Both-65+ couple (the central post-65 conversion scenario) keeps the deduction up to $350k.

Senior Bonus Deduction is available tax years 2025–2028 ONLY; SUNSETS after 2028 unless extended → the tax overlay must carry an explicit SUNSET MARKER (a calm note when an answer computed pre-2029 is viewed in/after 2029).

Engine tax + health scope decided 2026-06-04 ('the most complete picture'). IN the two-control solver's tax+health model: federal MFJ + single ordinary-income brackets; standard deduction (+ age-65 additions + senior-bonus deduction with phase-out & sunset); birth-year-derived RMDs (Uniform Lifetime); each year's withdrawal/conversion taxed as ordinary income stacked on that year's other ordinary income; Social-Security provisional-income taxation (the 'tax torpedo'); capital-gains / qualified-dividend stacking from taxable-account withdrawals; income-dependent healthcare — pre-65 ACA-PTC (400% FPL cliff is the 2026 base case, 'enhanced' = scenario toggle) and post-65 IRMAA (2-year MAGI lookback, distinct MAGI definition, hard cliffs). OUT-but-disclosed (candidate future levers next to the delta): NIIT (3.8% surtax) and state income tax — neither moves with sequencing or conversion.

Social-Security benefit taxation ('tax torpedo'): Provisional ('combined') income = AGI excluding SS + tax-exempt interest + 50% of SS benefits. MFJ tiers (fraction of benefits entering ordinary taxable income): provisional < $32,000 → 0%; $32,000–$44,000 → up to 50%; > $44,000 → up to 85% (single: $25,000 / $34,000). Exact inclusion follows the IRS Pub. 915 worksheet.

The SS provisional-income thresholds are NOT inflation-indexed — frozen since 1983 ($32k) / 1993 ($44k). They have NO vintage/staleness clock (unlike the brackets, which inflation-index annually): they are constants, not a dated fixture, and a frozen constant cannot go 'stale.' This is WHY more retirees are caught each year — a feature to model honestly, not a bug.

Computational landmine — the SS-tax circularity (a per-year FIXED-POINT, NOT a one-pass transform): taxable SS depends on provisional income, which depends on the year's other ordinary income — including the GROSS-UP withdrawal needed to cover spending + tax, which depends on the tax. The overlay resolves this per simulated year as a BOUNDED fixed-point (iterate provisional-income → taxable-SS → tax → gross-up to convergence, a few passes; deterministic, reads ZERO random draws — so still CRN-safe). The engine seam pins the convergence rule (iterate-to-stable or a fixed small pass count).

Not modeled (pending legislation): the proposed 'You Earned It, You Keep It Act' (would eliminate SS taxation) is NOT law as of 2026 — do not model speculative legislation; if enacted it becomes a Strand-5 update + a tax-vintage bump.

All of Strand 5 supports the two-control solver (withdrawal sequencing + Roth conversion) plus income-dependent healthcare. The survivor cliff is one driver among several, not the sole lever; the falsifiable IN/OUT line bounds the scope.

items.claim: What survives as a real gate is HONESTY HYGIENE on the recommendation copy across both controls: the headline must wear its probabilistic hedge (copyGuard's require-the-hedge lint), no false precision, and a wrong tax/health fact behind the verdict is the cardinal sin — the reset transferred the load onto honesty + engine validation, which get STRICTER for a recommender.

Constants discipline: every figure is keyed by year in the SINGLE canonical table and carries { value, citation, directionalUntilPinned }. A figure the research names but doesn't value is an Unsourced sentinel whose .value THROWS — never a plausible default. Full constants rules live in architecture.md; this doc supplies the numbers, that doc supplies the discipline.

Strand 3 (Regulatory) — ARCHIVE-AS-RATIONALE: The Back Nine is now a PERSONAL, non-commercial tool. Reg BI / the Investment Advisers Act govern compensated advice to clients; this product meets neither the relationship nor the compensation prong, so the whole strand is no longer a live constraint. Retained only as the documented WHY behind early v1 guardrails (no-verdict, no-optimizer, categorical-only triggers, the attorney-gate) so a future re-commercialization can re-instate them deliberately. Core finding preserved: the load-bearing defense was never the disclaimer — it was that a Roth-conversion what-if that names no securities is probably not 'advice about securities' at all (IAA §202(a)(11) Prong A threshold likely never closes); the counter-authority that made the no-verdict/calculator framing load-bearing is the SEC's Reg BI / 2019 RIA Interpretation (IA-5249) treating a Traditional-vs-Roth recommendation as an 'investment strategy involving securities.' Confidence was always defensible, not airtight (no on-point SEC no-action letter); the gate closed on securities drift (naming securities, asset-location advice, growth-rate-as-recommendation). Honesty descendants (certainty-hygiene, no-false-precision) survive on their own merits; nothing in this strand binds the current build.

items.claim: Strand 2 architecture decisions (build-shaping, still live): WASM + a single Web Worker clears a 1,000-path Monte Carlo sub-second (value is determinism + headroom, not raw speed). Non-extractable CryptoKey in IndexedDB is the canonical browser-E2E pattern. Recovery-phrase + mandatory-export with no provider password-reset for data is the zero-knowledge standard. Skip SharedArrayBuffer + COOP/COEP (single-threaded WASM in one worker is plenty, SAB is PWA-hostile). A non-extractable key is convenience, NOT the at-rest boundary (real protection is the encrypted blob + KDF). KDF: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 @ 600,000 iterations is the WebCrypto-native baseline; Argon2id-WASM (m=19456, t=2, p=1 or m=47104, t=1, p=1) only if the engine ever ships WASM (OWASP true fallback order Argon2id → scrypt → bcrypt → PBKDF2; salt = 16 random bytes, AES-GCM-256, extractable:false). Jazz DOWNGRADED (mid-rewrite to a 2.0 alpha API — foundation risk; Evolu less in-flux if sync is ever added). Recovery sharpened: SEPARATE login recovery from data-decryption recovery (raw research inverted this — the recovery phrase recovers BOTH; email/SMS reset is login-only and strands encrypted data); mandatory export at onboarding; treat IndexedDB eviction (WebKit ITP ~7-day clear) as best-effort so the exported phrase is the real durability backstop.

items.claim: Strand 1 (Voice-of-user UX pain) → thesis SUPPORTED. Across ProjectionLab, Boldin, Monarch, Empower, and Fidelity/Vanguard, dominant complaints are consumability failures, not capability gaps. The wedge: 'wildly different answers → distrust of any single number' (users run multiple tools, get results from 'good to retire' to 'much grimmer,' and stop trusting all of them; tools perceived as opaque black boxes). Users want 'permission and confidence,' not another precise-but-opaque number (synthesized insight, not a verbatim quote). Refinement: the hardest incumbent failure is DATA PLUMBING (account-sync breakage, aggregator duplicate cleanup) — a manual-first, local-first design sidesteps the whole class, so the thesis became 'consumability AND trustworthy data handling.' Honest caveat: the corpus is power-user / FIRE-skewed, so consumability pain for mainstream users is more likely understated than overstated.
